## R Markdown

This is an educational first attempt at a data driven website in R. This is a simplistic example of an R markdown based websie. This website explores the palmer penguins data set.

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)

penguins_big = penguins %>%
  filter(body_mass_g > 5000, bill_length_mm > mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex)) %>%
  group_by(island, sex) %>%
  summarise(max_weight = max(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE), 
            max_length = max(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), n())
print(penguins_big)

ggplot(data = penguins,
       aes(x = body_mass_g,
           y = bill_length_mm,
           color = sex,
           shape = island)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = F)

ggplot(data = penguins_big,
       aes(x = max_weight,
           y = max_length,
           color = island,
           shape = sex, na.rm = TRUE)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = FALSE)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
model_penguins = glm(formula = body_mass_g ~ species, data = penguins)
summary(model_penguins)
```
